variants.headline: Building job cancelled part-way
variants.sub: The client has abandoned {project}, which {builder} was building.
variants.body:
The building job for {project}, undertaken by {builder}, has been cancelled part-way because {why}. The client has given up the plan. Readers judging {target} should distinguish this cancellation from a completed handover and consider what responsible stewardship means when an undertaking ends with the work unfinished.

The gazette records cancellation during the work, rather than the completion of the building. The gazette favours fair treatment of {target} rather than an adverse verdict founded upon assumption alone.

variants.headline: Client abandons the construction plan
variants.sub: Construction of {project} by {builder} has been cancelled before completion.
variants.body:
The client has abandoned the plan for {project}, which {builder} was building. The reason given is that {why}. For {target}, the relevant question concerns the responsibilities attached to ending a building job part-way, rather than treating an unfinished undertaking as though nothing had ever been set in motion.

The gazette records cancellation during the work, rather than the completion of the building. The gazette favours fair treatment of {target} rather than an adverse verdict founded upon assumption alone.

variants.headline: Unfinished work meets a cancelled project
variants.sub: The building job for {project}, undertaken by {builder}, has been cancelled part-way.
variants.body:
Construction of {project} by {builder} has been cancelled, with {why} given as the reason. The client has given up the plan before completion. An assessment of {target} should keep the unfinished work in view without supplying a final financial settlement or a later use for the project.

The gazette records cancellation during the work, rather than the completion of the building. The gazette favours fair treatment of {target} rather than an adverse verdict founded upon assumption alone.
